requirements.title: List-directed records are values and separators with record-end and blank normalization
requirements.definition: List-directed records form a sequence of values and value separators; outside character constants, end of record acts as a blank and two or more consecutive blanks act as one blank.

S13.10.2-001 list-directed record normalization runtime fixtures: three complete internal READ programs use exact INTEGER and default CHARACTER observations. The two-record internal file ['1','2'] reads integers 1 then 2 because the record end acts as a blank; the single record '1   2' reads 1 then 2 because a run of blanks is one blank separator; and the record "'A  B'" reads CHARACTER(LEN=4) value 'A  B', with LEN checked explicitly so blank padding cannot hide lost embedded blanks. Feature mutations remove separators, reorder values, or alter the READ item count.

requirements.title: List-directed input values have null, constant, repeated-constant, and repeated-null forms
requirements.definition: A value is a null value, c, r*c, or r*; c and r have no kind type parameters; c is interpreted with the kind of the corresponding effective item; repeated forms are equivalent to successive constants or nulls and contain no embedded blanks except inside c where permitted.

pending.constant-value: Internal READ record '17' into default integer; expected value 17.
pending.no-kind-parameters: Deferred negative: record '1_4' as a list-directed integer value differs from the control '1' only by a kind type parameter in c; observe only a required input-error condition if the future Clause 12 owner supplies portable IOSTAT mechanics, not a compile-time diagnostic.
pending.no-embedded-blanks-in-repeat-form: Deferred negative: record '2 *5' differs from '2*5' only by an embedded blank in the r*c form; future fixture must isolate that input-error property.

The repeat-null case initializes [101,202,303], reads '2*' into the first two effective items, and requires all sentinels to remain [101,202,303]. No sentinel is zero.

requirements.title: List-directed value separators are comma or semicolon, slash, or qualifying blanks
requirements.definition: A value separator is the comma form (or semicolon in COMMA decimal edit mode), the slash form, or one or more blanks between nonblank values or after the last nonblank value.

pending.semicolon-separator-in-comma-mode: With DECIMAL='COMMA' supplied by the future Clause 12 owner, internal READ record '1; 2' into two integers; expected values 1 and 2. Without that mode this facet is not claimed.
pending.slash-separator: Internal READ record '1 / 99' into integer variables initialized to -1; expected first value 1 and following effective item unchanged through null-supply semantics owned by 13.10.3.2 p3.
pending.blank-separator: Internal READ record '1 2 ' into two integers; expected values 1 and 2.
